description_full: Tokyo Metro Co., Ltd. engages in the operation and management of railways in Japan. It is involved in the urban design and lifestyle creation businesses. The company also manages shops at stations and other commercial facilities; develops and rents office buildings and hotels; and provides advertising media services, such as advertisements in stations, premises and trains, and an information and communications business that handles licensing of mobile phone communication services, as well as leases optical fiber cable, etc. The company was formerly known as Teito Rapid Transit Authority and changed its name to Tokyo Metro Co., Ltd. in 2004. The company was founded in 1920 and is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.

financial_summary: TOKYO METRO CO LTD. is a mid-cap industrials business with a $5.1B market cap on $2.7B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +4.4pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 3% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $265M in free cash flow — roughly 10 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.27× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 6.1× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and interest coverage runs at 7.4×.

Shareholder yield of 4.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and within its sector the business captures 1.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
